# The auto-memory, mirrored

**Source of truth:** `~/.claude/projects/d--FGHackathon/memory/`. These files live outside the repository because that is where the memory mechanism reads them; editing this mirror changes nothing. Edit the source, then run `python CONTEXT/sync_context.py --write`.

**Why mirror them at all.** The memory files are loaded automatically, but only their one-line index is guaranteed to be in context. The full text matters when a rule has to be applied rather than merely recalled, and this is where a session that has lost its history can read all of it at once.

## `complete-agent-no-thresholds.md`

```markdown
---
name: complete-agent-no-thresholds
description: "Non-negotiable: the FortyGuard project must be a COMPLETE agent - no thresholds, no if-conditions deciding outcomes, no dashboard. Hackathon track wording is not an acceptable justification."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 6b457b07-2462-4797-9222-e8b3a1850b87
  modified: 2026-08-15T17:15:59.848Z
---

The user wants a **complete agent**, judged against a real definition of agency, not against what a
hackathon track will accept. Stated 2026-08-15, emphatically, with "Please never forget this":

> "i dont get what makes the system agentic and autonomous. I dont care much of what track 06 thinks
> makes a system agentic. I want a complete agent. No thresholds, if conditions or a simple dashboard."

**Why:** they are building this to be genuinely good, not to pass a checkbox. Earlier in the session I
argued that Track 06's wording ("analyze, decide, and automate ... without human intervention") sets a
lower bar than the sequential-decision bar the project had been failing, and offered that as a reason
to relax the requirement. **They rejected that reasoning outright.** Citing the track text, the judges'
backgrounds, or the rubric as a reason to accept weaker agency is not a valid argument to them, and
offering one costs trust.

**How to apply:** when claiming any part of the system is agentic, apply the falsifiable test the user
can check themselves - *can you point at the constant in the source code that produces this behaviour?*
If yes, it is a threshold in costume and must be labelled as such, not defended. Say plainly which
components are genuinely agentic and which are only computation. Never use the word "just" to wave
away a gap. Related: [[explain-at-beginner-level]].
```

## `diagnose-before-fixing.md`

```markdown
---
name: diagnose-before-fixing
description: "For any reported bug: report the measured cause before changing a line, and say which of the candidate explanations it actually is"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 7ee211e4-2d51-42ee-8d8a-f399d327e017
  modified: 2026-08-29T20:23:55.846Z
---

Stated 2026-08-30, on a tooltip rendering fault, with four candidate causes listed:

> "Diagnose before fixing. Do not guess. Inspect the implementation and tell me the actual cause.
> ... Report which it is before changing anything."

**Why:** the obvious reading of a UI symptom is often wrong, and a fix applied to the wrong cause
looks like it worked while leaving the real fault in place. On that occasion the reported symptom was
"the tooltip is semi-transparent"; the panel measured fully opaque, and the actual cause was a
`translate` on the hovered card creating a stacking context that trapped the panel's z-index, so a
neighbouring card painted over it.

**How to apply:** measure before editing, and measure the thing the symptom is about rather than the
thing that is easy to read. Computed styles are not paint order; `elementFromPoint` is not paint
order either. Get a real pointer and a real keypress in the loop when the state under test is
`:hover` or `:focus-visible` (`testing/cdp.py` in this repo exists for that), and back a DOM
assertion with a pixel assertion when the claim is about what a reader sees. Then state the cause,
with numbers, and only then change code. Companion to
[[prefer-smaller-defensible-figure]] and [[ship-production-not-mvp]].
```

## `explain-at-beginner-level.md`

```markdown
---
name: explain-at-beginner-level
description: "User is a second-semester CS student; define every technical term before using it, and never assume vocabulary from a reading plan they haven't finished"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 48b2e995-a9e0-4f0c-8ab4-8cbe4f628a17
  modified: 2026-08-04T17:41:59.037Z
---

Define jargon on first use, in plain language, before building on it. The user is a second-semester CS
student building the FortyGuard free-cooling agent solo. They asked twice to be explained things "like
I am a kid" after I used terms like METAR, hindcast, residual, calibration set, and effective sample
size as if they were shared vocabulary.

**Why:** they are studying conformal prediction, decision theory, and psychrometrics *while* building,
so a term appearing in their own project documents does not mean they know it yet. Unexplained jargon
made a document they had to act on unusable, and it stalled an approval.

**How to apply:** put a short glossary near the front of any document written for them; define a term
inline the first time it appears in prose; prefer a concrete analogy over a formal definition. They ask
sharp follow-up questions and will catch an overstated claim — when they push back, check whether they
are right before defending, and say plainly if they are.
```

## `live-agent-is-permanent.md`

```markdown
---
name: live-agent-is-permanent
description: "Never remove or relocate the live-agent card or its \"Run the agent on live data\" button from the demo's results stage"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: ce7469f0-426c-49a0-bdc6-a332de79e06e
  modified: 2026-08-27T17:43:14.001Z
---

The demo's live path — the `#livecard` panel at the results stage and its `#livego` button — is
permanent. Never remove it, never move it to another screen, and never replace it with a different
surface (a dialog, a masthead panel, a bezel control).

**Why:** stated directly on 2026-08-27 — *"dont ever remove the live agent working and its button
from there"*. Earlier the same day I had relocated the mode statement into a bezel lamp and added an
agent-link dialog with its own live controls; the response was that this "completely changed the
dynamic" and that the button had to be exactly where it was. Mentioning that both static and live
modes must keep working is a CONSTRAINT on UI work, not a request for new live features.

**How to apply:** treat `#livecard`, `#livego`, `probeLive()`, `drawModeBanner()`,
`drawLiveUnavailable()`, `drawLiveCost()` and `runLive()` as fixed. UI/UX work may restyle them —
colour, type, the disabled state's appearance — but must not change where they are, what they are,
or what they say. If a live-path change seems necessary, ask first.

Serving matters and is easy to get wrong: `python -m http.server` is a static server, so
`/api/health` 404s and the button correctly disables itself with "Live agent not attached". The live
button only enables under `python AGENTIC-ARBITER/src/serve_live.py`, and only actually spends with
`--allow-paid` (4,220 credits per hourly window, so 50,640 for a 12-hour horizon). Never start a
plain static server and leave it as "the demo is running". See [[ship-production-not-mvp]] and
[[complete-agent-no-thresholds]].
```

## `no-em-dashes.md`

```markdown
---
name: no-em-dashes
description: Never use em dashes in any copy written for this project; keep the masthead to a header plus 2-3 lines
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Never use an em dash (—) in copy written for this project. Said directly on 2026-08-28: *"Never use
ehmm dashes"*. Applies to page copy, README prose, commit messages and anything else a reader sees.
En dashes and the horizontal bar are out for the same reason; ordinary hyphens in compound words
(hour-by-hour, ground-mounted) are fine.

**Why it is worth obeying rather than treating as taste:** an em dash is the easiest way to bolt a
second thought onto a finished sentence, and it was doing exactly that in three of the four masthead
paragraphs. Removing them forces one thought per line, which is most of what made that block
shorter.

**Related and stated in the same breath:** the masthead is a header plus **2 to 3 lines**, not four
paragraphs. It is the first thing on screen and it was pushing the specification plate, which is
where the measured numbers are, below the fold on a laptop. When prose has to go somewhere, use the
`.info` popover pattern already in the page: the claim stays on the same element one interaction
away, and it sits in the trigger's `aria-label` so it is not lost to a reader who cannot hover.

⚠ The ORIGINAL copy deeper in the page still contains many em dashes the user wrote themselves. They
were not swept. Ask before rewriting those; this rule governs what I write.
See [[live-agent-is-permanent]] and [[project-renamed-agentic-arbiter]].
```

## `prefer-smaller-defensible-figure.md`

```markdown
---
name: prefer-smaller-defensible-figure
description: "When a headline number could be big-and-modelled or small-and-measured, ship the small one and label any modelling in the UI itself, not in a popover"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 7ee211e4-2d51-42ee-8d8a-f399d327e017
  modified: 2026-08-29T18:59:49.223Z
---

Stated 2026-08-29, on the two portfolio summary cards:

> "A per-site figure multiplied by the site count is a modeled projection, not a measurement.
> Presenting one as fact is unacceptable. Judges will ask how it was derived, and an unlabeled
> extrapolation does more damage to credibility than a smaller honest number. If in doubt, prefer
> the smaller defensible figure."

Plus: **inspect the data layer and report which aggregates can be computed directly BEFORE choosing
what to display**, and report back the exact computation and source for every number shown.

**Why:** the whole product's claim is that its figures are checkable. One number a judge can pull
apart costs more than every impressive number gains, and the user has to be able to defend each one
live.

**How to apply:** when two framings of the same fact are available, pick the one that needs no
asterisk, and put the caveat on the card in words rather than behind an `.info` popover. Worked
examples from that day: shipped 4,232,006 hours of weather (98 stations counted once) rather than
10,820,547 site-hours; headlined chiller-hours rather than dollars, because hours need no tariff,
no power density and no state; and printed "238 of 250 sites gain hours, the 12 that lose are
subtracted" and "189 of 250 priced on a Virginia/Illinois reference" directly on the card.
Companion to [[ship-production-not-mvp]] and [[complete-agent-no-thresholds]].
```

## `project-renamed-agentic-arbiter.md`

```markdown
---
name: project-renamed-agentic-arbiter
description: The project is AGENTIC-ARBITER; it was INTAKE-ARBITER until 2026-08-27, and the folder is AGENTIC-ARBITER/
metadata:
  type: project
---

The project is **AGENTIC-ARBITER**. It was called INTAKE-ARBITER until 2026-08-27, when it was
renamed at the user's request — they wanted the word "Agentic" in the name, short and impressive, and
chose AGENTIC-ARBITER from four options.

The rename covered every surface: the folder `AGENTIC-ARBITER/`, 2,737 string occurrences across
2,649 text files, the split bezel wordmark (`Agentic·Arbiter`, which is two spans and so invisible to
a literal search), and all 266 generated report PDFs — those were REGENERATED with `report.py`, never
byte-patched, because a PDF's xref table is byte-offset addressed and the new name is one byte longer.

**Two things deliberately keep the old name, and both are records rather than code:** the build
`*.log` / `*.err` files at the repo root (a log is a transcript of what was printed at a past moment;
rewriting one makes it a transcript of something that never happened) and `report (7).pdf` at the
repo root, which is a stray browser download rather than a generated artefact.

An empty `INTAKE-ARBITER/src/` husk may still exist: the editor's file watcher held a handle on the
directory, so the children were moved out individually and the shell could not delete the last empty
directory. It is safe to delete once the editor releases it. See [[live-agent-is-permanent]].
```

## `react-app-is-the-deliverable.md`

```markdown
---
name: react-app-is-the-deliverable
description: "The React app is the product; verify the URL a visitor opens, not demo/index.html"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: ce7469f0-426c-49a0-bdc6-a332de79e06e
  modified: 2026-08-28T16:20:07.526Z
---

**The React app in `AGENTIC-ARBITER/app/` is the deliverable. `demo/index.html` is the reference
implementation it was lifted from, not the thing being shipped.** When checking anything about the
front end, check what a visitor gets at the deployed root, not the single-file page.

**Why:** the user has had to say this more than once, most sharply on 2026-08-28: *"it is rendering THE
PREVIOUS HTML FILE VERSION OF UI. i have told you a million times that we are dealing with the react
UI."* They were right. `serve_live.py` served `demo/` as its static root, so `/` returned
`demo/index.html` while the React bundle sat at `/app/`. Build green, bundle current, key present,
wrong page. I had spent the preceding effort on intermittent `no-server` 404s and never checked which
page the SUCCEEDING requests returned.

**How to apply:** when a check passes and the user still sees the old thing, suspect the layer the
check does not cover. "The bundle is current" and "the bundle is what `/` returns" are different
claims, and only the second is what the user is looking at. Assert on the response, at the URL a
visitor opens. `run_all.py` step 33 now does this; trap 5b.6 records the reasoning.

Both front ends still exist on purpose, so this is about PRIORITY, not deletion. See
[[live-agent-is-permanent]] and [[ship-production-not-mvp]].
```

## `ship-production-not-mvp.md`

```markdown
---
name: ship-production-not-mvp
description: "Non-negotiables for the FortyGuard build — a fully functioning end-to-end product on a genuine high-impact problem, with textbook-correct conformal prediction, never an MVP or prototype"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 734850ff-07bb-4d9a-9735-24e94a6d6b71
  modified: 2026-08-18T17:18:49.609Z
---

Stated 2026-08-18 as **non-negotiable for the entire rest of the build**:

1. **Not an MVP, not a prototype — a fully functioning end-to-end solution.** "It demonstrates the
   idea" is not acceptable as a stopping point.
2. **The problem must be a genuine urban-heat problem with real impact and commercial value.** Not a
   toy framing chosen because it was tractable.
3. **Conformal prediction must be done as it is supposed to be done**, so the agent's output is
   rigorous and win-worthy. Marginal-only coverage applied outside its calibration domain is not
   acceptable. Group-conditional (Mondrian) + adaptive (ACI/DtACI) is the standard to hit, and the
   distribution-free *conditional* impossibility result must be stated rather than papered over.
4. **Every claim in `AGENTIC-ARBITER/PLAN.md` carries a real citation with a link**, verified by
   opening the source — never from a search snippet.
5. **Wire FortyGuard's data in deeply, not as a crumb.** Use the environmental parameters that
   genuinely change the physics or the decision, with a cited reason for each.

**Why:** they are entering a hackathon judged on Impact 40 / Technical 35 / Innovation 15 /
Communication 10 plus Business Viability, and they intend to win rather than participate. A
demo that only gestures at the idea loses to one that runs.

**How to apply:** when a shortcut would leave a stage stubbed, simulated, or statistically
unjustified, build the real thing instead — and if something genuinely cannot be built in the time,
say so explicitly and in full rather than shipping a hollow version of it. See
[[complete-agent-no-thresholds]] for the companion rule on agency, and
[[explain-at-beginner-level]] for how to report it.
```

## `subagents-permitted.md`

```markdown
---
name: subagents-permitted
description: "Rule 9 (no subagents/workflows) was lifted 2026-08-23 — parallel agents are allowed, but their findings are leads, not results"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 9cbe198d-7b6c-4879-b664-294d58c80b18
  modified: 2026-08-23T13:19:59.785Z
---

On 2026-08-23 the user lifted the FGHackathon project's standing "rule 9": *"eliminate rule 9 and
use subagents/workflows or Task tools when needed."* Subagents, Task tools and Workflows are now
permitted. The rule had been honoured across every prior session and is documented as lifted in
`HANDOFF.md` §1 rule 9 and §9.-1 item 5.

**Why:** the project is large enough that finding defects one at a time is the bottleneck — the
user had already said as much once before, in effect *"stop finding these one at a time"* (the
per-site sweep in `HANDOFF.md` §10). Parallel search is the right tool for a tree with ~30 source
modules, a 406 KB handoff and a dozen shipping documents.

**How to apply:** delegate SEARCH and independent VERIFICATION; never delegate the judgement.
Every other project rule still binds a subagent exactly as it binds the main session — especially
"no unverified claims" and "ask before every paid FortyGuard call." Confirm any subagent finding
against the actual artefact before it reaches a document or a fix; a fan-out that returns plausible
prose is the project's own gotcha #47 ("my verification code was buggier than the product") at N
times the volume. See [[ship-production-not-mvp]] and [[complete-agent-no-thresholds]] for the
standards a delegated result still has to meet.
```

## `two-day-pairs-deferred.md`

```markdown
---
name: two-day-pairs-deferred
description: "Two measured FortyGuard day-pairs are deliberately not in the published figures, and run_all.py therefore does not exit 0"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ce7469f0-426c-49a0-bdc6-a332de79e06e
  modified: 2026-08-28T08:21:20.715Z
---

On 2026-08-28 the user deferred adopting two measured FortyGuard day-pairs (2026-08-25, 2026-08-26)
that exist as tracked fixtures but are absent from every published figure: *"dont do it right now,
we'll do it later. just save the pairs somewhere for now."*

**Why:** adopting them moves the headline honesty number from 65.6 % to 78.6 % bound coverage and the
n/(n+1) ceiling from 80 % to 85.7 %, which means restating README lines 119, 278 and 363 and
regenerating 243 artefacts plus 266 PDFs. The 90 % promise is unmet either way. Changing a headline
figure is the user's call, not mine.

**How to apply:** do not rebuild artefacts or restate figures until they say so. Two consequences to
hold in mind: `run_all.py` currently fails two steps (it rebuilds with six pairs, then audits against
docs quoting four), while `audit.py` alone still passes 2,216/0 on the committed set. And `run_all.py`
and `build_sites.py` REWRITE `AGENTIC-ARBITER/demo/` in place, so a run leaves 243 files whose numbers
contradict the published ones; `git checkout -- AGENTIC-ARBITER/demo/` restores them. Never read a
figure off the tree during or after a partial run.

Full evidence and the measured before/after table are in `CONTEXT/01-STATE.md` section 5. Related:
[[context-folder-is-the-source]], [[ship-production-not-mvp]].
```
